topic: Choose a database technology for the new analytics project

scenario.topic: Choose a database technology for the new analytics project
scenario.opening_question: What balance of performance, scalability, and ease of use should we prioritize for our analytics database?

options.name: Amazon Redshift Data Warehouse
options.upside: Highly scalable and integrates well with AWS analytics tools
options.tradeoff: Requires expertise to optimize performance and manage clusters
options.concern: Potential vendor lock-in and costs may rise with usage spikes
options.best_for: projects needing scalable, performant SQL analytics with cloud integration

options.name: PostgreSQL with TimescaleDB Extension
options.upside: Open source with strong time-series support and familiar SQL interface
options.tradeoff: May require manual tuning and hardware scaling for large data volumes
options.concern: Could face performance bottlenecks as data grows beyond medium scale
options.best_for: teams valuing cost efficiency and ease of development with time-series data

options.name: Google BigQuery Serverless Analytics
options.upside: Serverless with no infrastructure management and excellent scaling
options.tradeoff: Costs can be unpredictable depending on query complexity and frequency
options.concern: Data ingestion latency and potential vendor dependency
options.best_for: projects prioritizing minimal maintenance and elastic scalability

options.name: Apache Cassandra NoSQL Cluster
options.upside: Excellent write throughput and fault tolerance for distributed data
options.tradeoff: Limited ad-hoc query capabilities and steeper learning curve
options.concern: Not ideal for complex analytical queries requiring joins or aggregations
options.best_for: use cases needing high availability and write-heavy workloads

shared_context: The analytics project must handle up to 10TB of data with daily batch updates
Budget for database licensing and maintenance is capped at $50,000 per year
The decision group consists of exactly 3 participants with mixed expertise in data engineering and analytics

personas.background: Nadia has experience with cloud-native analytics platforms and values scalable, serverless solutions for rapid data insights.
personas.private_goal: She prefers a minimal maintenance, highly scalable analytics platform that can handle elastic workloads efficiently.

D) Apache Cassandra NoSQL Cluster — annual cost: $20,000; ease of use: low; query latency: low (milliseconds for key-based lookups) (+ Excellent write throughput and fault tolerance for distributed data; − Limited ad-hoc query capabilities and steeper learning curve)
